nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Aglaia: Means "splendor, beauty, brightness" in Greek. Aglaia was one of the Three Graces in the Greek mythology (with Euphrosyne and Thalia).
- elaeagnoidea: From Greek eleagnos, referring to a local tree: myrica or sweet gale

stem_bark.text: The bark of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is reddish-brown and smooth.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is reddish-brown and smooth.

seed.text: The seed of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is ovoid and solitary. This seed is coated with a white and thick (edible) pulp.
seed.text_html: The seed of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is ovoid and solitary. This seed is coated with a white and thick (edible) pulp.

fruit.text: The fruit of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is a berry . This berry is globose to ovate and 1 to 1.5 cm across. The fruit of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is buff-coloured turning orange when ripe, tomentose and 1-seeded.
fruit.text_html:
The fruit of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is a berry.
This berry is globose to ovate and 1 to 1.5 cm across.
The fruit of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is buff-coloured turning orange when ripe, tomentose and 1-seeded.

flower.text: The inflorescence of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is an axillary panicle . This panicle is pyramidal and 6 to 10 cm long. The flowers of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are 2-3 mm across, yellow-coloured. The calyx is composed of 5 tiny, tomentose and yellow sepals. The yellowish corolla is composed of 5 ovate and imbricate petals (1.5 mm long and 1 mm wide). There are 5 stamens and the ovary is globose and 2-celled. The buds of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are green. The flowers are fragrant.
flower.text_html:
The inflorescence of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is an axillary panicle. This panicle is pyramidal and 6 to 10 cm long.
The flowers of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are 2-3 mm across, yellow-coloured.
The calyx is composed of 5 tiny, tomentose and yellow sepals.
The yellowish corolla is composed of 5 ovate and imbricate petals (1.5 mm long and 1 mm wide).
There are 5 stamens and the ovary is globose and 2-celled.
The buds of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are green.
The flowers are fragrant.

images.caption: Aglaia elaeagnoidea inflorescence at the axil of a new leaf

leaf.text: The leaves of Aglaia elaeagnoidea grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaves have a 2.5 to 3.5 cm long petiole. The leaflets of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are imparipinnate (2-3 pairs of opposite leaflets), dark green coloured above and pale green beneath. They are glabrous on both sides and coriaceous. The leaflets are 5-10 cm long and 2-4 cm wide. They are elliptic to oblanceolate, the apex is acute (sometimes obtuse), the base is cuneate and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is reticulate.
leaf.text_html:

The leaves have a 2.5 to 3.5 cm long petiole.
The leaflets of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are imparipinnate (2-3 pairs of opposite leaflets), dark green coloured above and pale green beneath. They are glabrous on both sides and coriaceous.
The leaflets are 5-10 cm long and 2-4 cm wide. They are elliptic to oblanceolate, the apex is acute (sometimes obtuse), the base is cuneate and the margins are entire.
The venation of the leaf is reticulate.

habit.text: Aglaia elaeagnoidea is a medium sized evergreen tree . It is densely branched and foliaceous attaining a height of 15 m.
habit.text_html: Aglaia elaeagnoidea is a medium sized evergreen tree. It is densely branched and foliaceous attaining a height of 15 m.

ecology.text: Aglaia elaeagnoidea is a canopy tree in evergreen forests up to 1000 meters. Aglaia elaeagnoidea is sometimes found as an understorey tree in wet evergreen forests ( www.biotik.org ).
ecology.text_html:
• Ecology :

    Aglaia elaeagnoidea is a canopy tree in evergreen forests up to 1000 meters.
    Aglaia elaeagnoidea is sometimes found as an understorey tree in wet evergreen forests (www.biotik.org).

reproduction_dispersal.text: Aglaia elaeagnoidea is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Aglaia elaeagnoidea is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Aglaia elaeagnoidea is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Aglaia elaeagnoidea is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.

phenology.text: From November to March. From May to October. From July to October. Evergreen ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )
phenology.text_html:
• Flowering season :

    From November to March.

  • Fruiting season :

    From May to October.

  • Seeding season :

    From July to October.

  • Leaves falling :

    Evergreen

    • (This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains)

culinary.text: The white and acid pulp surrounding the seed of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is edible. Source : Basu, B.D., K.R. Kirtikar & I.C.S., 1918, Indian Medicinal Plants. Bahadurganj, India, Sudhindra Nath Basu, Panini office
culinary.text_html:
The white and acid pulp surrounding the seed of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is edible.

Source : Basu, B.D., K.R. Kirtikar & I.C.S., 1918, Indian Medicinal Plants. Bahadurganj, India, Sudhindra Nath Basu, Panini office

medicinal.text: The fruit of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is cooling, astringent, tonic, antidiarrheal, anti-inflammatory and it is also used for treating skin diseases. The seeds of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are used for painful urination. Source : Chopra, R.N., 1956, Glossary of Indian medicinal plants. Council of Scientific & Industrial Research
medicinal.text_html:
The fruit of Aglaia elaeagnoidea is cooling, astringent, tonic, antidiarrheal, anti-inflammatory and it is also used for treating skin diseases.

The seeds of Aglaia elaeagnoidea are used for painful urination.

Source : Chopra, R.N., 1956, Glossary of Indian medicinal plants. Council of Scientific & Industrial Research

reforestation.text: Aglaia elaeagnoidea is able to grow in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. The tree can be planted in half shade. This tree is propagated by seeds. 12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Aglaia elaeagnoidea is able to grow in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. The tree can be planted in half shade.
    This tree is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
